Because this weaker acid undergoes only slight ionization compared to the complete ionization of the strong acid, the solution pH changes much less drastically than it would in an unbuffered solution [ev_007].

replay.question: How do simple diffusion and facilitated diffusion differ?

released_response.answer_text: Both simple diffusion and facilitated diffusion are passive transport processes in which substances move down their concentration gradient from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration without expending cellular energy [ev_002]. They differ primarily in how substances cross the cell membrane [ev_001]. In simple diffusion, substances pass freely and directly through the lipid bilayer [ev_001] [ev_013]. In contrast, facilitated diffusion is used for substances that cannot cross the lipid bilayer directly due to their size, charge, or polarity, requiring transmembrane proteins such as protein channels or carrier proteins to assist their movement across the membrane [ev_001] [ev_002] [ev_013].

Invalid uploaded assets. Reject unsupported/disguised types, unsafe paths and configured oversize input. No failed upload becomes a ready document or retrievable chunk; valid inputs remain usable.

Quality blockers. Blocked/empty/unreadable units produce an inspectable quarantine state. Publication requires explicit resolution or documented exclusions; warnings and original counts remain visible.
Idempotent ingest and revisioned processing. Repeated raw upload reuses the asset version. Changed rules create a processing run/new release as appropriate; old answer/evidence content is unchanged.

Embedding and vector correctness. Known vector fixtures return expected ranking. Wrong dimensions, non-finite vectors or missing chunk embeddings prevent release publication rather than producing a partially valid index.

E0 remains an evaluation condition. In both benchmark schemas it calls no retriever and has no evidence/history/profile/gold. MCQ candidate choices belong only to MCQ; openQA has no choices. Shared model settings are recorded.

Grounded conversational answer. A natural-language message produces ChatResponseV1 prose and valid current-context citations. Trace user message→context/profile→prepared query→release/chunks→model attempt→saved assistant response. No A–D fields are required.

Appropriate insufficient-evidence handling. A clear factual request with no usable evidence gets a useful grounded refusal. A greeting or missing-referent clarification is not rejected for lacking textbook citations. Retrieval/system failures remain errors rather than empty-success refusals.

Mode-specific validation. Reject invalid chat JSON/types/citations without extracting arbitrary A–D labels. Validate option-text equality only for MCQ. Finite repair preserves errors; a schema failure is not a normal refusal.

Provider timeout and retry bounds. Injected timeout/429/transient failures respect configured call/time caps. Permanent auth/configuration failures do not loop; no silent provider/model switch occurs.

Submission idempotency. Same user/key/body returns the original job; the same key with a changed body returns conflict. Duplicate clicks and concurrent submissions do not duplicate a logical question or paid execution.

Lean worker interruption recovery. Interrupt the single worker and restart. Persisted work recovers or fails explicitly within bounded rules; stale/cancelled attempts cannot publish. Uncertain external execution is reported, not promised exactly once.

Ownership and source visibility. Another user’s resources are inaccessible; learners cannot administer. Deactivated sources disappear from new retrieval and revoked historical evidence is unavailable with an explanation.

Per-turn profile snapshots. Conflicting updates return conflict; an in-flight reply retains its snapshot. Later profile changes affect later turns only. A failed new response cannot overwrite an existing successful assistant message.

Browser continuity. Refresh/re-login restores persisted jobs, history and accurate answer states. Evidence is keyboard-usable; retryable failures preserve drafts and feedback edits do not duplicate records.

SciQ adapters are deterministic and separate. MCQ shuffling/labels reproduce with the same seed. OpenQA sends stem only, excluding distractors/correct answer/support. No SciQ support is indexed as a textbook; evaluator references never appear in provider input.

Correct protocol denominators. Freeze all scheduled items, retain refusals/errors/cancellation, and reconcile results separately for openQA, MCQ and conversations. Hand-calculated EM/F1/accuracy/retrieval examples agree; provisional runs are labelled.

Experiment and rating honesty. Frozen manifests cannot be edited in place; variant differences are inspectable. Missing qrels/ratings remain null, repeated attempts are not cherry-picked and no mock score becomes a live claim.

Local backup/restore and packaging. Restore to a disposable environment and verify users, active release and evidence hashes. Distributable artifacts exclude credentials and unapproved source content; no disaster-recovery certification is implied.

Chat-first dependency logic. No missing IDs or cycles across 108 tasks. G4 includes actual history and profile-enabled conversation, without waiting for a completed G5 SciQ run or G7 blind ratings. G8 regresses all six journeys.

Shared components, explicit mode differences. Instrument chat, openQA and MCQ submissions to verify one answer service/retrieval/model/persistence implementation. The plain standalone no-profile chat and openQA paths share the free-form engine; distinct response adapters are not fake equivalent outputs.

Lean evaluator-only gold storage. API/answer-worker runtime lacks the evaluator-only gold files/store credentials. Submissions require valid frozen run/item references and strict gold-free DTOs; public endpoints cannot retrieve labels.

Tail-request retry lifecycle. A failed latest turn creates one new job for the same request, preserving terminal history and counters. A non-tail failed turn cannot inject a late replacement into later conversation; no duplicate user message or published answer.

Finite preparation/generation budgets persist. Query preparation, answer calls, transient retry/repair and worker restart retain aggregate totals. Ordinary chat is not forced into a second teaching call; offline study jobs use explicit individual limits.
Actual release rollback. Activate A, then B, then validated/intact A as rollback. Exactly one active pointer remains. Invalid/missing/unavailable rollback targets are rejected while B stays usable.

Frozen-run environment changes. Deactivate/revoke a source during a frozen run. Stop affected new calls, retain prior outcomes and mark the environment change; do not silently change the corpus under the same comparison.

Processing-run provenance. Reprocess unchanged raw bytes with a different chunker. The raw version is reused, processing identity changes and releases/annotations refer to exact chunk sets; old spans/evidence remain intact.

Embedding replacement boundaries. Change embedding configuration and verify compatible cache keys, dimensions and a newly built release. Reject mixed dimensions and preserve historical evidence hashes without rewriting unrelated product modules.

Real follow-up reference resolution. Ask a concept question, then “Why does it need light?” with an appropriate prior topic. Inspect actual included messages, standalone query and model prompt; the correct referent is used without exposing the evaluator answer.

Useful clarification and social turns. In a new chat, “Why does it do that?” asks for the missing topic; “Hello” gets a brief greeting. Neither requires fake options or citations. The next user clarification continues the same conversation.

Topic change and correction. Switch from one science topic to another and correct an earlier premise. The prepared query prioritises the new topic/correction, does not carry irrelevant citations, and does not treat prior assistant errors as verified facts.

Re-explanation with actual evidence reuse. Request simplification/example/summary of the previous reply. Reused source text is available, actually passed to this request and assigned new local IDs; old ev_001 cannot point to a different passage. Revoked sources are explained as unavailable.

Bounded long history. Exceed the recent-turn window, build a versioned extractive summary of the older prefix and keep important referents. Assert combined token limits, cutoff, no duplicate prefix and deterministic fallback. Missing old context yields clarification, not invented recall.

Session isolation and resumption. Re-login restores the same session and response revisions. A new or another user’s session has no old transcript/summary; the current user’s explicit saved profile may apply by policy. No cross-session accidental reference resolution.

Real chat UX and terminal states. Enter/Shift+Enter, copy, follow-up suggestions, composing/progress, cancellation, failure draft retention and keyboard citations work through real endpoints. No fake stream or successful unpersisted assistant message is displayed.

Latest-answer revisions. Regenerate only the latest completed response; preserve its old revision and feedback until the replacement succeeds. Failed replacement leaves it visible, concurrent repeats deduplicate, and subsequent prompts use the selected current revision.

Open-answer execution without hidden choices. The SciQ-derived stem enters ChatResponseV1 through the free-form engine with no correct answer/distractors/support/profile/history. MCQ runs separately with four candidates. Changing evaluator references cannot change generation inputs.

Lexical proxies cannot masquerade as semantic correctness. Test negation, minus signs, numbers/units, missing compact answers and legitimate paraphrases. EM/F1 use the frozen compact-answer rules, not whole-explanation substring search; full-response review and MCQ metrics remain separate.

Existing-work migration and effective spec audit. Upgrade a fixture containing old MCQ records without losing users/history/citations; new chat has no required choices and uses real context. Check active docs/diagrams/task states/client schemas and preserve old evidence as historical, not v3 acceptance.

New live prompts contain no OPTION_A hook. Changing evaluator gold, coverage or evidence_status leaves system-visible payloads unchanged; MCQ option presentation is symmetric.
A natural message with no choices reaches chat. MCQ alone requires exactly A–D and rejects missing/normalised duplicate options. Match MCQ option text exactly; never extract letters from chat prose.
Reject duplicate keys, Markdown fences, multiple objects, trailing garbage, NaN/Infinity, invalid null/types and extra fields in new modes. Accept valid objects and preserve stable error codes.
For new ChatResponseV1 refusal and MCQ refused=true, require confidence=null with their respective empty/null and citation rules. Invalid output remains an error, not a refusal.
finish_reason=length is not publishable merely because text is nonempty. Empty choices or missing message/content yield standard provider errors, not unhandled IndexError.

Missing provider/key configuration is explicitly unavailable, without mock fallback. A historical probe remains one past connectivity record; configuration examples do not become frozen or verified providers.
